text:
The Blues paid two first-round picks (15th and 29th) at the 2026 draft to bring Mason McTavish over from Anaheim, and 23 games in, he looks like the shooter they bought. He's getting 1.43 expected goals per 60 (the quality of the looks he gets), up from 1.22 last season, and his 8 goals on 8.8 expected are right where they should be.

The last ten games have been quieter: three points where we'd expect about six at his ice time, though the chances he's on the ice for haven't dropped. That reads more like a dry spell than a decline. Saturday's breakaway power-play goal against New Jersey, off one of Jake Neighbours' five assists, was a reminder of the finish.

The question from Anaheim follows him. Evolving-Hockey had him driving offense last season (86th percentile among forwards) and leaking chances the other way (bottom 2%), and the Blues get 48.9% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man. Our range puts him at 19 to 32 goals.
